title: Kth Missing Positive Number
pattern: count of missing values as a monotone function
problemStatement: Given a strictly increasing array of positives, find the k-th missing positive integer.
intuition: At index i, the number of missing values before a[i] is a[i] - (i+1) — monotone non-decreasing. Binary search for the first index where this count reaches k.

approaches.title: Brute: walk the naturals
approaches.idea: Scan the array, decrementing k on each gap.
limitations: Fine for small n, but the interviewer usually asks for O(log n)

approaches.title: Optimal: binary search on the missing count
approaches.idea: missing(i) = a[i] - (i+1); find the boundary and offset.
approaches.dryRun:
a=[2,3,4,7,11] k=5
missing: 1,1,1,3,6
first index with missing >= 5 is 4, so lo=4 -> answer 4+5=9
approaches.whyWorks: After the loop, lo is the count of array elements below the answer, so answer = lo + k.

edgeCases: k smaller than the first gap -> answer is k
commonMistakes: Returning a[lo] instead of lo + k
patternRecognition: Derive a monotone counting function, then binary search it
followUps: k-th missing in an unsorted array
interviewInsight: The final `lo + k` step is unintuitive; derive it from the invariant rather than memorising it.
